title: ValueTask and when it is appropriate
description: Understand ValueTask allocation semantics, when it improves performance, and when it hurts.

data.text: `Task<T>` is a reference type. Every time you create one, the heap allocates an object. In hot paths, these allocations add up and increase garbage collection pressure. `ValueTask<T>` offers a way to avoid allocations when the result is already available.

`ValueTask<T>` is a struct that can wrap either a `T` result or a `Task<T>`. When the result is already computed, it holds the value directly — no heap allocation. When the result is not ready, it wraps a `Task<T>` and allocates as needed.

data.title: ValueTask with cached result

items: **High-frequency methods** — APIs called thousands of times per second benefit most from allocation savings.
**Often-complete results** — Cached or already-computed values that complete synchronously.
**Performance-critical paths** — Inner loops, parsing, or custom async enumerables.

data.text: `ValueTask<T>` has important restrictions. It should not be awaited multiple times, and it should not be used with `Task.WhenAll` or `Task.WhenAny` unless you convert it to a `Task<T>` first. Using it incorrectly can cause subtle bugs or performance regressions.

items: Do not await a `ValueTask<T>` more than once.
Do not store a `ValueTask<T>` in a field or local for later use.
Convert to `Task<T>` with `.AsTask()` when mixing with `Task` combinators.
Measure before optimizing — `ValueTask<T>` adds complexity that is not always justified.

data.title: ValueTask is not a drop-in replacement
data.text: Changing a public API from `Task<T>` to `ValueTask<T>` is a breaking change for consumers. Only use `ValueTask<T>` when benchmarks prove the allocation savings are significant.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: ValueTask avoids heap allocations when the result is already available.
Use it for high-frequency, often-synchronous operations.
Do not await it multiple times or store it for later.
Convert to Task when using Task combinators.
